the use of context information in one-to-one marketing can be made privacy-aware by providing customers with the ability to control the collection, storage and usage of their context information.

the deployment of one- to-one marketing services that do not collect any personal data, but solely use context information, can increase customer acceptance and thereby the success of one-to-one services in stationary retail.
the privacy of customers can be preserved by allowing customers to control the usage of their personal data and by providing them with personalized and relevant services based on context information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how one-to-one marketing can be realized in stationary retail without violating the customer's privacy.
providing a framework that allows for one-to-one marketing to be deployed in stationary retail, while preserving customers' privacy.
the question: how can one-to-one marketing be provided in stationary retail without violating customers' privacy?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
one-to-one market-ing in stationary retail and customer privacy do not constitute an antagonistic pair.
the use of context information to provide one-to-one marketing is feasible and can be done in a privacy-aware fashion.
privacy and one-to-one marketing do not necessarily conflict with each other, and that it is possible to provide one-to-one services in stationary retail without violating customers' privacy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
one-to-one personalization in retail can be achieved by using context information, but the customers' privacy should be respected and controlled by the customers.

one-to-one services can be provided in stationary retail, if the privacy of the customer is taken into consideration and if the customer is allowed to actively participate in the collection and usage process.
the privacy of the customers can be protected by providing them with the possibility to control their personal information and to be informed about its use.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the deployment of one-tomarketing in stationary retail can be realized in a way that respects the privacy of customers.
the use of context information for one-to-one marketing is feasible, and can be accepted by customers.

one-to-one services can be provided to stationary retail customers in a privacy-aware manner, and that customers are willing to accept such services if they can control the collection and the usage of context information.
